Volumetric Analysis Acidimetry and Alkalimetry Acidimetry and alkalimetry is related with the measurement of strength of an acid or an alkali in presence of each other.
Volumetric Analysis It is a quantitative analysis in which the strength of an unknown solution is determined by taking standard solution with the help of known volumes of these two solutions.
Note: Gravimetric analysis is related to determination of toeight.
Unknown solution is such a solution whose strength is to be determined.
Standard solution is such a solution whose strength is known to us.

E.g. N/ IO (decinormal) NazC03 solution. Standard solutions are of two types: i) Primary standard solution: It is the solution prepared by dissolving known weight of solute having certain characteristics into a known volume/ weight of solution/ solvent. A substance used to prepare primary standard solution is called primary standard substance, and should have following requisites:
It should be available in pure and dry state. a)
The composition of the substance should not change. That b) is, it should not have very good oxidising or reducing behaviour. Similarly, it should not be excessively hygroscopic or deliquescent.
Substance with high equivalent mass is preferred to minimise the possible errors due to weighing.

Practical Chemistry Examples: anhydrous Na2C03, crystals of oxalic acid, Mohr's salt [FeS04 (NH4)2 S04 6H201 etc. ii) Secondary standard solution: The solution which has been standardised with the help of a primary standard solution is called secondary standard solution. It represents the number of gram equivalent of solute dissolved in per litre of its solution.
If one gram equivalent of solute is dissolved per litre of its solution, then the solution is called normal solution (1 N).
